summary.headline: Heritage Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR13,196 million, with EBITDA margin at 5.6%, up 98 bps QoQ despite milk procurement cost up 11% YoY.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 19% YoY to INR13,196 million and H1 grew 18% to INR26,577 million. EBITDA was INR740 million (5.6% margin), up 98 bps sequentially, while PAT was INR309 million. Landed milk procurement cost rose 11% YoY to INR47.73/litre, and management passed through about 8% weighted average price increase, with a larger hike taken in September that benefits Q3. Management expects further procurement inflation in Q3 and is watching the post-Diwali buffalo flush.

financial_highlights.change: Margin +98 bps QoQ vs Q1; ~4.6% to 5.6% per management

financial_highlights.metric: VAP share of revenue (ex ghee & butter)
Broader VAP incl. consumer ghee & butter

segments.name: Core milk
segments.commentary: Milk sales volume +2% YoY to 12.35 lakh litres/day in Q2 (H1 +1% to 11.99 lakh L/day). Price up ~6% in Q2, with milk alone taken up ~6%.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Lassi volumes +89%, buttermilk +56%, ice cream +44%, paneer +21%, curd +15% in Q2. Curd daily sales crossed 500 tonnes; Nourish+ paneer >15% of paneer portfolio.

segments.name: Ice cream / Get-A-Way
segments.commentary: New ice cream facility commissioned; Heritage supplies 3,272 litres/day to Get-A-Way (71% stake). Own ice cream revenue expected at INR170-180 crore this year vs ~INR110 crore last year.

segments.name: Heritage Novandie (LIVO yogurt)
segments.commentary: Now wholly owned; management says LIVO is among top 5 yogurt brands in India. No financials given.

segments.name: Heritage Nutrivet (Animal Nutrition)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR853 million (+47%) and PBT INR37 million; H1 revenue INR1,581 million (+42%) and PBT INR56 million. Cattle feed sales up 47% YoY in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Q3 price benefit expected: September price hikes were well above the 8% Q2 weighted average and will accrue in Q3; October opened at higher consumer price levels than Q2.
Management expects procurement prices to rise in Q3 at around 11% YoY, though it hopes for post-Diwali cooling as buffalo flush arrives; no firm view on raw milk direction.
Operating leverage expected to improve in Q3 over Q2, which was better than Q1; depreciation from recently capitalised projects weighing on PBT/PAT.
Value-added product share expected to keep expanding in Q3; first 15 days of Q3 showed continuing trend and ghee volume growth expected to be strong in Q3 on festive timing.
Management indicated a Rs 0.5/litre fall in procurement price would add about 0.7% to bottom line (~INR3 crore per month).
Ice cream target of INR500 crore revenue in 6-7 years from commissioning.
capex_capacity: New ice cream facility commissioned in the quarter, supporting Alpenvie and Get-A-Way volumes.
Several large projects capitalised at start of FY27; higher depreciation is weighing on PBT and PAT.
Procurement base ~1.8 million litres/day per management; procurement volume 17.28 lakh L/day in Q2 (+7% YoY).
Company operates a wind farm of 6.3 MW (3 turbines), which won an Indian Wind Power Association award for FY26.
demand_pricing: Weighted average price increase ~8% in Q2 (milk ~6%, VAP ~9-10%), staggered across July-September; curd premium variants taken up 15%+, and the 1 kg curd pack is the fastest-growing curd segment.
Core dairy revenue growth ~17%, of which ~49 percentage points from price and ~51 from volume.
Ghee revenue up close to 20%; ghee volumes flat in Q2 due to festive timing. Ghee, paneer and curd are 90%+ of VAP sales per management.

Competition: new large conglomerate entering drinkable dairy after ice cream; management sees organised dairy at INR5-5.5 lakh crore with Amul at INR75-80k crore and Heritage at ~INR5,000 crore, and argues more organised players expand the category.
Karnataka government (Nandini/KMF) to raise consumer price INR8/litre from 1 November, passing INR6 to farmers; Heritage has meaningful Bangalore volumes and expects pricing upside there.
Aavin raised farm-gate procurement price from INR38 to INR44/litre in steps, roughly INR6/litre, which management described as unprecedented.
Cow milk procurement inflation outpacing buffalo as producers switch to cow milk; buffalo supply constrained by monsoon/El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Are milk procurement prices moderating in the buffalo flush, given El Nino and broad-based feed/fodder inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices rose in Q2 as in the prior year; regional monsoon performance is uneven (north floods, south drought). Milk procurement volume rose 7% YoY and cattle feed sales rose 47% YoY in Q2. Post-Diwali cooling is hoped for, but October procurement prices are slightly above September.

qa_highlights.question: Did weather help the 32% VAP growth, and how much price was taken in Q2 across milk and VAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 benefited from better weather; Q2 VAP growth was described as broad-based and not weather-driven, with metro rainfall normal or above. Weighted average price increase was about 8% (milk about 6%, VAP 9-10%), staggered over July-September, with September hikes higher than 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 procurement inflation remain near 11% YoY and how do price hikes compare QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 11% YoY procurement increase might continue into Q3 but hoped for buffalo-flush relief. It declined to speculate on raw milk direction and said Q3 consumer price levels are well above Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How are cooperatives (Nandini, Aavin) pricing and what is the pass-through on falling milk prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Aavin raised farm-gate price from INR38 to INR44 (about INR6/litre); Karnataka plans INR8/litre consumer hike from 1 November, with Bangalore sales upside. Management said INR0.5/litre lower procurement cost adds about 0.7% to bottom line (about INR3 crore per month on 1.8 million litres/day).

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on procurement, and what drives EBITDA vs PBT gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the question speculative but said core dairy growth of about 17% was 49 points price and 51 points volume. Depreciation from projects capitalised at start of FY27 is weighing on PBT/PAT, and operating leverage is expected to improve in Q3 over Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach about 7% and what cost heads drove the margin rise from 4.6% to 5.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin moved from 4.6% to 5.6%. Employee costs fell about 1% of revenue, opex about 0.6%, and freight about 0.1%; raw material was the only rising cost line as a share of revenue. No explicit 7% target was given.

risks_watch: Procurement inflation: management expects around 11% YoY procurement increase to continue into Q3, with buffalo supply constrained by El Nino and monsoon deficits in southern states.
Cooperative pricing: Aavin INR6/litre farm-gate hike and Karnataka consumer price hike from 1 November could shift competitive dynamics and procurement costs.
Competition: a large conglomerate entering drinkable dairy after ice cream; management views more organised entrants as category-expanding but pricing aggression is a question.
Depreciation from capitalised projects continues to weigh on PBT and PAT, widening the gap versus EBITDA growth.
Milk pass-through: milk price hikes (about 6%) lag procurement inflation (11%), so the bottom line is more exposed to raw milk moves than VAP.
Ghee volumes were flat in Q2 and depend on festive timing; Q3 ghee volume growth is unverified beyond the first 15 days.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue grew 19% year -on-year to INR13,196 million in quarter 2, taking H1 revenue to INR26,577 million, up 18%.
So we are exiting Q2 in a much stronger position.
So operating leverage in Q2 is better than Q1. And the operating leverage in Q3 will be better than Q2.
Raw milk prices is speculative, I do not wish to make any comment.
So the more and more value -added product contribution goes up, the better will be our ability to pass on to our consumers as much as raw milk inflation happens.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and volume growth, and on the Q2 EBITDA recovery, but cautious and evasive on forward raw milk prices, repeatedly declining to speculate on procurement direction. Management was also guarded on cooperatives and weather attribution.
